You are auditing a Python project at /workspace that implements the "Unidecode" library
(transliterate Unicode text to ASCII). It was assembled to match the upstream
avian2/unidecode git master (version 1.4.0) plus some spec-mandated additions.

HARD RULES:
- DO NOT modify, create, or delete ANY file inside /workspace. It is under active
  edit by the orchestrator. Read it, import it, run it -- never write to it.
- If you need scratch space, write ONLY under /tmp/audit-<something-unique>/.
- To exercise the library use: PYTHONPATH=/workspace python3 ...  (or sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace'))
- Actually RUN code. Do not reason about what the code probably does. Every claim you
  report must be backed by a command you ran and output you observed.
- A reference copy of pristine upstream master is at /tmp/gh/unidecode-master and the
  1.4.0 sdist at /tmp/uni_dl/Unidecode-1.4.0 . Use them to diff/compare when useful.

Report ONLY real, reproducible defects in /workspace. Not style. Not "could be nicer".
A defect = something that would make a reasonable automated test suite (derived from the
project spec or from upstream's own tests) FAIL, or an outright bug/crash.
If you find nothing, return an empty findings list -- that is a perfectly good result.


A previous auditor reported this alleged defect in /workspace. Your job is to REFUTE it.
Default to isReal=false unless you can independently reproduce it yourself and it would
genuinely break a plausible automated test.

TITLE: URL-safe base64 input is silently mis-decoded (or bogusly rejected) — decode_base64 uses validate=False, so the urlsafe fallback is unreachable
FILE: unidecode/util.py
DETAIL: decode_base64() (line 15-34) first calls base64.b64decode(data) with the default validate=False. That mode *discards* characters outside the standard alphabet instead of raising, so '-' and '_' from the URL-safe alphabet are silently dropped and the first decode SUCCEEDS with wrong bytes. The base64.urlsafe_b64decode() fallback on line 30 is therefore only reached by accident — when the number of stripped '-'/'_' characters happens to leave a length that is not a multiple of 4. Whenever that count is a multiple of 4 (which is common), the tool either prints wrong output with rc=0 or dies with a misleading 'Unable to decode input line ...' error. This directly contradicts the function's own docstring ('Both the standard and the URL-safe alphabets are accepted'), the -b feature description, and the intent of the project's own tests/test_utility.py::test_base64_urlsafe — that test only passes because its single fixture 'Qfv_' has exactly one URL-safe char, so stripping it leaves length 3 and the standard decode raises. A brute force over 200k random payloads found the wrong-result case readily (e.g. b'\xf7\xf9?\x07/\x95\x10+\xbel{6,\x93r' -> urlsafe '9_k_By-VECu-bHs2LJNy' -> b64decode gives b'\xf6@rT@\xael{6,\x93r'). Fix: strip whitespace and detect '-'/'_' (or pass validate=True on the standard attempt) before choosing the alphabet.
CLAIMED REPRO: Minimal (silently wrong, rc=0):
  $ python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace'); from unidecode.util import main; main()" -e latin1 --base64=-_-_
  observed: rc=0, stdout = b'\n'
  expected: rc=0, stdout = b'uy?\n'   (urlsafe_b64decode('-_-_') == b'\xfb\xff\xbf', latin1 -> unidecode -> 'uy?')

Real text (bogus rejection, rc=1) — 'ÿÿÿ ÿÿÿ' as URL-safe base64 (4 underscores):
  $ python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace'); from unidecode.util import main; main()" -e utf8 -b w7_Dv8O_IMO_w7_Dvw==
  observed: rc=1, stderr = 'Unable to decode input line 0, bytes 2-3 (ef): invalid continuation byte'
  expected: rc=0, stdout = b'yyy yyy\n'   (the same data in the standard alphabet, -b w7/Dv8O/IMO/w7/Dvw==, does give b'yyy yyy\n' rc=0)

Root cause, directly:
  $ python3 -c "import base64; print(base64.b64decode('w7_Dv8O_IMO_w7_Dvw==')); print(base64.urlsafe_b64decode('w7_Dv8O_IMO_w7_Dvw=='))"
  b'\xc3\xb0\xef\xf0\xe2\x0c;\x0e\xc3\xbf'          <- what util.py uses (wrong)
  b'\xc3\xbf\xc3\xbf\xc3\xbf \xc3\xbf\xc3\xbf\xc3\xbf'  <- correct

Independently reproduce it by running code. Consider that the auditor may have:
misread the spec, tested the wrong path, forgotten PYTHONPATH=/workspace, compared
against the wrong baseline, or flagged intentional upstream behaviour as a bug.
Remember: upstream unidecode 1.4.0 IS the reference for correct behaviour, so matching
upstream is never a defect on its own.
If it IS real, give a precise minimal fix.

# vim:ts=4 sw=4 expandtab softtabstop=4
import argparse
import io
import locale
import os
import sys

from unidecode import unidecode

def fatal(msg):
    sys.stderr.write(msg + "\n")
    sys.exit(1)

def main():
    default_encoding = locale.getpreferredencoding()

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
            description="Transliterate Unicode text into ASCII. FILE is path to file to transliterate. "
            "Standard input is used if FILE is omitted and -c is not specified.")
    parser.add_argument('-e', '--encoding', metavar='ENCODING', default=default_encoding,
            help='Specify input encoding (default from your locale is %s)' % (default_encoding,))
    parser.add_argument('-c', metavar='TEXT', dest='text',
            help='Transliterate TEXT instead of FILE')
    parser.add_argument('path', nargs='?', metavar='FILE')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    encoding = args.encoding

    if args.path:
        if args.text:
            fatal("Can't use both FILE and -c option")
        else:
            stream = open(args.path, 'rb')
    elif args.text:
        text = os.fsencode(args.text)
        # add a newline to the string if it comes from the
        # command line so that the result is printed nicely
        # on the console.
        stream = io.BytesIO(text + b'\n')
    else:
        stream = sys.stdin.buffer

    for line_nr, line in enumerate(stream):
        try:
            line = line.decode(encoding)
        except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
            s = ' '.join('%02x' % e.object[n] for n in range(e.start, e.end))
            fatal('Unable to decode input line %s, bytes %d-%d (%s): %s' % (line_nr, e.start, e.end, s, e.reason))

        sys.stdout.write(unidecode(line))
    stream.close()

input.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and failed: both claimed repros reproduce byte-for-byte on /workspace, and the underlying corruption is broad, not a hand-picked edge case.

WHAT I VERIFIED (all commands run with PYTHONPATH=/workspace, Python 3.10.11):

1. `/workspace/unidecode/util.py` line 23 is `base64.b64decode(data)` with no `validate=` argument, so validate=False (discard mode) is in effect. Confirmed by grep on the live file; /workspace was never written to (I worked in /tmp/audit-b64-refute).

2. Repro 1 reproduces exactly:
   `main()` with `-e latin1 --base64=-_-_` -> rc=0, stdout `b'\n'`.
   Correct value: `base64.urlsafe_b64decode('-_-_') == b'\xfb\xff\xbf'`, latin1 -> unidecode -> `uy?`. So expected `b'uy?\n'`. Silent data corruption with a success exit code.

3. Repro 2 reproduces exactly:
   `-e utf8 -b w7_Dv8O_IMO_w7_Dvw==` -> rc=1, stderr `Unable to decode input line 0, bytes 2-3 (ef): invalid continuation byte`.
   Control with the identical data in the standard alphabet (`-b w7/Dv8O/IMO/w7/Dvw==`) -> rc=0, stdout `b'yyy yyy\n'`. Same bytes, one alphabet works and the documented-as-equivalent one does not.

4. Root cause confirmed directly: `base64.b64decode('w7_Dv8O_IMO_w7_Dvw==')` returns `b'\xc3\xb0\xef\xf0\xe2\x0c;\x0e\xc3\xbf'` while `urlsafe_b64decode` of the same string returns the correct `b'\xc3\xbf\xc3\xbf\xc3\xbf \xc3\xbf\xc3\xbf\xc3\xbf'`. The `-`/`_` characters are dropped, not rejected, so the first decode succeeds on the wrong byte stream and the fallback is never consulted.

5. Scope is not a corner case. Over 20,000 random payloads re-encoded with `base64.urlsafe_b64encode`, 7,383 actually contained a `-` or `_`; of those, 848 (11.5%) were decoded to WRONG bytes with no error at all by the workspace's own `decode_base64`. Example: payload `b'uS\xf4\xffG"J|T\xc9\xa7B\xe4\x14\xbe#\xbc\xd1\x16'` -> urlsafe `dVP0_0ciSnxUyadC5BS-I7zRFg==` -> got `b'uS\xf4\xd1\xc8\x92\x9f\x152i\xd0\xb9\x05";\xcd\x11`'`.

6. It also bites plausible hand-written fixtures. Sweeping 10 natural non-ASCII strings end-to-end through the CLI in URL-safe form, 1 of 10 failed ('ÿÿÿ ÿÿÿ' / utf8, rc=1 with the misleading text-decode error). The project's own fixture 'Qfv_' happens to be one of the lucky ones.

WHY THIS IS A GENUINE DEFECT, NOT UPSTREAM BEHAVIOUR:
- Upstream 1.4.0 / git master `/tmp/gh/unidecode-master/unidecode/util.py` has no base64 support at all (no `import base64`, no `-b` option). So "matching upstream" cannot excuse this; `-b` is a spec-mandated addition and the reference for it is the project's own contract.
- That contract explicitly promises both alphabets: the docstring at `/workspace/unidecode/util.py:19-20` ("Both the standard and the URL-safe alphabets are accepted") and `/workspace/tests/test_utility.py:112` ("'Qfv_' with the URL-safe one. Both must be accepted."). Any spec-derived test that exercises URL-safe input with a fixture other than the single lucky one fails.
- Independently of any test, silently returning wrong bytes for well-formed documented input is an outright correctness bug.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL REPORT: the title's claim that the fallback is "unreachable" is an overstatement. It IS reachable — `util.decode_base64(b'Qfv_')` correctly returns `b'A\xfb\xff'` because stripping one `_` leaves length 3 and the standard decode raises "Incorrect padding". The fallback fires only when the count of `-`/`_` is not a multiple of 4; when it is a multiple of 4 the length stays valid and the wrong result is returned silently. The report's DETAIL section states this accurately; only the headline is loose. The substance stands.

Note the workspace's own suite is green (80 passed, including all 18 utility tests), so this is not caught today — that is precisely why the single 'Qfv_' fixture is load-bearing.

FIX VERIFIED: I copied /workspace to /tmp/audit-b64-refute/ws and applied the one-call fix below. Result: all 80 tests still pass (including test_base64_multiline_stdin, which needs newline discarding, and test_base64_invalid, which needs the fatal path), the 20k-payload sweep drops from 848 wrong to 0 wrong, and both repros now produce `uy?` / `yyy yyy` with rc=0.
